issues.title: Gaussian covariance evolution
issues.failure_explanation: For the affine drift in the proof, the covariance identity requires the transpose partner Σ_t C_{*,t}^{-1}P_t. The old lemma instead claims Σ_t P_t C_{*,t}^{-1}. For a concrete admissible case, take target covariance I, initial covariance R=[[2,1],[1,2]], constant preconditioner C_{*,0}=diag(1,2), and β=κ=1. Then P_0=(I+R^{-1}+C_{*,0}^{-1})^{-1}=(1/34)[[13,2],[2,16]], and the old cross-term P_0C_{*,0}^{-1}R+RP_0C_{*,0}^{-1} equals (1/34)[[55,25],[29,35]], which is nonsymmetric. A covariance derivative must be symmetric, so the stated ODE and its proof calculation are false without an additional commutativity assumption.
issues.overall_effect: The general covariance ODE in the Gaussian-moments lemma is invalid for noncommuting covariances and preconditioners, although the Gaussian closure and mean equation remain intact. Later uses specialize to commuting or scalar products, where the two orders coincide, so no later formal result is affected by this particular root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the covariance cross-term in the Gaussian-moments lemma by P_t C_{*,t}^{−1}Σ_t + Σ_t C_{*,t}^{−1}P_t. In the proof, apply the standard linear-SDE identity dΣ_t/dt = A_tΣ_t + Σ_tA_t^T + 2C_{*,t}, so the second drift factor is transposed. The Gaussian closure and mean equation remain unchanged, and no later commuting or scalar specialization requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes a genuine covariance-propagation error by omitting a transpose, so this is not merely a transcriptional typo. Nevertheless, the standard linear-SDE covariance identity gives a short, uniquely determined local repair requiring no new lemma or construction and causing no loss of scope or guarantee. There are no affected dependent formal results, and the later specializations use commuting matrices for which the two orders coincide.
